This page monitors local traffic only: VpnService creates a TUN interface (10.8.0.1/32) on this device and the system routes local IPv4 traffic through it. Traffic from other devices on the same Wi-Fi is not visible — that requires root + ARP spoofing or NIC promiscuous mode, which ordinary Android apps do not have.

HTTPS content is end-to-end encrypted; only the TLS SNI domain and destination IP are visible (TLS 1.3 ECH hides the SNI). Plaintext HTTP is required to see Host and path; DNS queries are visible unless DoH / DoT is used. The HEX dump keeps only the first 64 bytes of each packet, never the full payload; all statistics come from real packets.

Sessions aggregate bidirectionally by (source IP, destination IP); protocol mix and domains are accumulated across the whole session. The packet list keeps only the latest 500 packets, so its row count may be lower than the summary total. Top domains and peers are sorted by packet count, then by name.

To keep the network up, the service forwards flows in user space: UDP / TCP each open a protected upstream socket, and replies are re-encapsulated and written back to the TUN, which adds slight latency. ICMP is not forwarded (failing ping is expected), and IPv6 does not traverse this tunnel. Idle flows are reclaimed after 60 seconds; long-silent TCP connections may be dropped.

Stopping monitoring first writes to a self-pipe to wake the read thread, then closes the TUN fd; the system removes the VPN icon from the status bar and restores direct connectivity. The read, cleanup and forwarding threads are all daemons with join timeouts and never block service teardown.
